connections.observation: `s002` shows φύλαξ shifting from guarding the city to guarding a δόγμα to guarding oneself. `s010` shows δόγμα first as the conviction each guardian holds (τοῦ παρʼ αὑτοῖς δόγματος) and then as the rulers' decrees (τῶν ἀρχόντων δόγμασιν) that auxiliaries serve. Held together, the two sequences make visible a movement from internal conviction guarded by the self to authoritative decrees guarded by others, articulating a spatial and hierarchical transfer of what δόγμα names and who guards it.

`s005` presents three modes of involuntary loss—theft, enchantment, force—each explained in sequence. `s004` shows γοητεύω recurring through this explanation and crystallizing in the compound δυσγοήτευτος. Together they make visible that enchantment, the middle term of the three-part sequence, generates its own lexical family and testing vocabulary (γοητείας ἅμιλλαν, δυσγοήτευτος), while theft and force do not.

`s008` shows βασανίζω appearing first in the gold-in-fire comparison and immediately after in the lifelong testing. `s009` shows χρυσός first as the tested metal in fire and then as the metal mixed into rulers' souls. Together they make visible that the simile's two elements—testing (βασανίζω) and gold (χρυσός)—separate and each enters a different subsequent context: testing becomes the biographical sequence of age-stages, gold becomes the ontological claim of the noble lie.

`s003` shows φύλαξ shifting from self-guarding to complete external/internal guarding to the metallic φύλαξ whose guarding destroys. `s018` contrasts external enemies (ἔξωθεν πολεμίων) with internal friends (ἐντὸς φιλίων), differentiated by will versus capacity to harm. Together they make visible that complete guardianship (φύλακας παντελεῖς) articulates a spatial opposition (ἔξωθεν/ἐντός) that collapses in the prophecy, where the φύλαξ is qualified not by spatial origin but by metallic nature (σιδηροῦς, χαλκοῦς), and guarding itself inverts into destruction.

`s013` narrates formation under the earth, upward release, and earthborn identity. `s021` shows πλάττω appearing first for the fashioning under the earth and then for the god fashioning with metals. Together they make visible that the spatial movement (ὑπὸ γῆς ἐντός, then ἀνῆκεν upward) corresponds to a shift in the agent of πλάττω from passive formation in the earth to active divine fashioning, both occurring before the upward release that completes the mythic birth.

`s011` shows πείθω clustering around the noble lie. `s012` shows ψεῦδος recurring with the interlocutor's naming of Socrates' shame. `s019` shows hesitation, shame, fear, and boldness clustering at the lie's introduction. Together they make visible that persuasion (πείθω, πειθοῦς) and falsehood (ψεῦδος, ψευδομένους) occur in immediate lexical proximity at 414b–c, surrounded by a vocabulary of affect (ὀκνέω, ᾐσχύνου, τόλμα, μὴ φοβοῦ) that marks the threshold of uttering the lie as itself a tested moment requiring boldness.

`s014` shows kinship language clustering in the noble lie: earth as mother and nurse, citizens as brothers and kin. `s015` shows κήδομαι appearing early as rulers caring for what they love and returning at the close as the lie's purpose—to make citizens care for city and one another. Together they make visible that the kinship vocabulary (μήτηρ, τροφός, ἀδελφοί, συγγενεῖς) supplies the mythic ground for the closing κήδεσθαι, so that care (κήδομαι) first articulated through love and shared interest (412d) is re-grounded through fabricated blood relation.

`s007` shows four metals assigned to social roles, with ὑπο- compounds naming concealed metallic nature in offspring. `s003` shows the metallic φύλαξ (σιδηροῦς, χαλκοῦς) whose guarding would destroy the city. Together they make visible that the metals, initially distributed hierarchically (gold to rulers, silver to auxiliaries, iron and bronze to producers), converge in the prophecy as the two lowest metals (σίδηρος, χαλκός) whose elevation to guardianship marks civic destruction, inverting the hierarchical distribution into a configuration of ruin.

`s017` shows a life-sequence from children through youths and men to the living and the dead. `s008` shows βασανίζω recurring first in the gold-in-fire simile and then in lifelong testing across the same age-stages. Together they make visible that the biographical sequence (παισί, νεανίσκοις, ἀνδράσι) is twice articulated—once as the span of testing (βασανιζόμενον) and once as the span of honors extending beyond death (ζῶντι καὶ τελευτήσαντι, τάφων, μνημείων)—so that the same life-course receives both ordeal and reward.

`s001` shows ἄρχω/ἄρχων recurring from the initial question of who will rule and be ruled, through qualifications for rulers, to the noble lie where gold is mixed into those fit to rule. `s002` shows φύλαξ shifting across contexts from guarding the city to guarding conviction to guarding offspring's natures. Together they make visible that the section moves from distinguishing rulers (ἄρχοντες) and guardians (φύλακες) as separate questions (412b–c) to a final configuration where complete guardians (φύλακας παντελεῖς, 414b) and rulers (ἄρχοντες) are presented together, and guardianship itself becomes layered: guarding externally and internally, guarding δόγμα, guarding self, and guarding offspring.

`s020` shows Socrates proposing to persuade first the rulers, then the city, and the interlocutor answering that the rulers themselves cannot be persuaded, only their sons and later generations. `s011` shows πείθω recurring around the noble lie with πεῖσαι appearing three times at 414c–d. Together they make visible that persuasion is named repeatedly at the moment of utterance but immediately acknowledged as impossible for the present generation, so that the lie's persuasive efficacy is deferred to sons (ὑεῖς) and later people (οἱ ὕστερον), displacing successful πειθώ from the speaking present into generational futurity.

`s006` contrasts voluntary and involuntary departure of opinion, assigning false opinion to the voluntary and all true opinion to the involuntary. `s005` lists three involuntary modes—theft, enchantment, force—each explained separately. Together they make visible that the involuntary loss of true opinion is not a single event but a threefold structure differentiated by agent and means: time or argument steals (κλαπέντας), pleasure or fear enchants (γοητευθέντας), pain or suffering compels (βιασθέντας), so that ἀκουσίως names a triad, not a unity.

`s016` identifies the lie as Φοινικικόν τι, explicitly not new (μηδὲν καινόν), something poets claim happened elsewhere but not in the speakers' time. `s011` shows the poets having persuaded (πεπείκασιν) of such events. Together they make visible that the lie is introduced through a double relation to poetry: poets have already performed successful persuasion (πεπείκασιν) of this type of story, but the story has not occurred in the speakers' own time (ἐφʼ ἡμῶν δὲ οὐ γεγονός), so that poetic persuasion provides the model while temporal distance marks the lie's novelty in the immediate context.

`s001` shows ἄρχω/ἄρχων moving from the question of who will rule through qualifications to the noble lie where those fit to rule receive gold. `s007` shows four metals assigned hierarchically and the ὑπο- compounds naming concealed metallic offspring. Together they make visible that the capacity to rule (ἱκανοὶ ἄρχειν, 415a) is no longer established through testing and δόγμα-guarding but through divine mixing of gold at birth (χρυσὸν ἐν τῇ γενέσει συνέμειξεν), and that the rulers' primary task shifts from self-testing to offspring-inspection (φυλάξουσι … τοὺς ἐκγόνους, 415b), so that ruling becomes a matter of natal metal and generational vigilance rather than biographical ordeal.

elements.form: ὡς ἐν τύπῳ, μὴ διʼ ἀκριβείας
elements.context: ἡ ἐκλογὴ εἶναι καὶ κατάστασις τῶν ἀρχόντων τε καὶ φυλάκων, ὡς ἐν τύπῳ, μὴ διʼ ἀκριβείας, εἰρῆσθαι

new_signals.observation: Immediately after the lifelong testing sequence concludes, Socrates qualifies the entire preceding account of selection and establishment as spoken in outline (ἐν τύπῳ), not in precision (μὴ διʼ ἀκριβείας). This marks the threshold between the testing procedure and the noble lie that follows.

elements.context: ὑπὸ γῆς ἐντὸς πλαττόμενοι καὶ τρεφόμενοι
ἃ ἡμεῖς αὐτοὺς ἐτρέφομέν τε καὶ ἐπαιδεύομεν
ὡς περὶ μητρὸς καὶ τροφοῦ τῆς χώρας

new_signals.observation: τρέφω appears first as the educators' action (ἐτρέφομεν), then as the mythic underground nurture (τρεφόμενοι), then in the noun τροφός naming the earth. The lie reassigns the nurturing agent from the speakers to the earth.

elements.context: ὥσπερ ὀνείρατα ἐδόκουν ταῦτα πάντα πάσχειν τε καὶ γίγνεσθαι περὶ αὐτούς

new_signals.observation: The education and nurture just described are to be recast as dream (ὀνείρατα), with the underground fashioning presented as the truth (τῇ ἀληθείᾳ). This inverts the epistemic status of the preceding account.

elements.context: ὡς χρησμοῦ ὄντος τότε τὴν πόλιν διαφθαρῆναι

new_signals.observation: The prophecy (χρησμός) that the city will be destroyed when an iron or bronze guardian guards it is introduced without attribution, presented as an authoritative oracle embedded within the myth.

elements.context: τὴν τῇ φύσει προσήκουσαν τιμὴν ἀποδόντες

new_signals.observation: τιμή appears twice in immediate succession at 415c: first as the honor owed to nature when demoting offspring (ἀποδόντες, ὤσουσιν), then as the act of honoring when promoting offspring (τιμήσαντες, ἀνάξουσι). Demotion and promotion are both named through τιμή.
